tool.name: Logan Protein Search
tool.description: Search a database (FAISS or usearch) using pre-computed embeddings
tool.command: if [ -n "\$GALAXY_LOGAN_PROTEIN_SEARCH_FORCE_CPU" ]; then FORCE_CPU="--force_cpu"; else FORCE_CPU=""; fi && mkdir results && ln -s '$query_sequences' query_sequences.fasta && python /app/search_database.py --query_sequences query_sequences.fasta --database '$database_sel.database.fields.path' --output results/ --db-type '$database_sel.database_type' #if $outfmt: --outfmt '$outfmt' #end if --num_threads "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-16}" --memory "\${GALAXY_MEMORY_MB:-16000}" \$FORCE_CPU

param.name: query_sequences
param.label: Original query sequences
param.help: FASTA file containing the query sequences

validator.message: This tool accepts exactly one query sequence. The selected FASTA file contains a different number of sequences. Please check your inputs.

param.name: database
param.label: FAISS Database
param.help: Select a pre-built FAISS protein database to search against

validator.message: No FAISS protein database is available for version @TOOL_VERSION@ of this tool. Please ask your Galaxy administrator to install a database built for this version.

param.name: outfmt
param.label: MMseqs2 output format
param.option: BLAST tabular, plus query and database sequence lengths (2)

tool.help:
## **Logan Protein Search**
**What it does**
Searches for homologs of a query protein in a pre-built database of Logan proteins, using the gLM2 protein language model instead of classical sequence comparison. Because the search happens in embedding space, it can find remote homologs that sequence-similarity searches miss.
The tool takes a **single protein sequence** and returns the related Logan50 protein clusters, the proteins they contain, and MMseqs2 alignments of those proteins against the query.
This is a **single-step** tool: it embeds the query itself, so no separate embedding step is required.
Embedding is now built in - the *Embed Query Sequences* tool is only needed if you want the embeddings themselves.
-----
**Inputs**
- **Original query sequences** - a FASTA file containing the query. This must be **protein** sequence, and must contain **exactly one sequence**. Datasets with more (or fewer) sequences are rejected by the tool form. - **Database Type** - whether to query the *usearch* or the *FAISS* vector database. - **FAISS Database** - a pre-built database of embedded Logan proteins. Only databases built for this exact tool version are listed, because an index is not compatible across versions. If the list is empty, ask your Galaxy administrator to install a database for this version.
-----
**Parameters**
- **MMseqs2 output format** - the format of the alignment output. The options are:
| Mode | Format | | ------ | -------- | | 0 | BLAST tabular (default; a column header line is prepended) | | 1 | SAM | | 2 | BLAST tabular, plus query and database sequence lengths | | 3 | Pretty HTML | | 4 | BLAST tabular, with column headers |
-----
**Outputs**
- **Diversified hits (TSV)** - the Logan50 proteins whose gLM2 embedding lies within a cosine distance of 0.2 of the query embedding. Four columns: query name, result name, result sequence and cosine distance:
``` #query_name result_name result_sequences cosine_distance alpha ERR11474596_7103_1 MLDWNTSSDIF... 0.015888094902038574 ```
- **Matched proteins (FASTA)** - the proteins that actually align to the query according to MMseqs2. This is usually the output of interest, and is a subset of *All similar proteins*.
- **MMseqs2 alignments** - alignment details for those proteins, in the format selected above. With the default mode 0 the columns are target, query, identity, alignment length, mismatches, gap openings, target start/end, query start/end, e-value and bit score.
- **All similar proteins (FASTA)** - every Logan protein contained in the matched Logan50 clusters. Many of these do **not** align to the query with MMseqs2, so this set is broader and noisier than *Matched proteins*.
